chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Musa ibn 'ibn 'Imran from his uncle Al-Husayn 'ibn 'Isa 'ibn Abdillah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said:

My father took my hand, then said: 'O my son, indeed my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) took my hand just as I took your hand, and said: 'Indeed my father Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) took my hand and said: 'O my son, do good to everyone who seeks it from you. If he is deserving of it, then you have hit its mark; and if he is not deserving of it, then you are deserving of it. And if a man insults you from your right, then turns to your left, and apologizes to you, accept his apology.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on responding to insults and showing kindness to others?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Imams in *Al-Kafi*, establishes a continuous chain of ethical instruction emphasizing proactive benevolence (*ihsan*) and patience (*sabr*) in social interactions. It teaches that doing good to those who ask is always correct, and if they are worthy, the reward is secured; if not, the giver still merits the reward. It further advises accepting apologies from those who insult you, demonstrating high moral character.
